Subject: Next steps: SDK POC + environment roadmap for BrightPath

Hi Emily / Simon —

Thanks again for the productive call earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can get a small SDK proof-of-concept running quickly and validate embedding/reranker + structured output flows for your triage/search use case.

Summary of needs we heard:
- Local developer quickstart (Python + TypeScript) to validate integrations and latency profiles.
- Authentication: you mentioned wanting federated login (OIDC) and short-lived tokens instead of static API keys for dev and staging.
- Routing: ability to route by region and fail over to hosted model variants if on-prem capacity is hit.
- Embeddings + reranker: semantic search across patient notes (PHI).
- Structured output / tool calling: triage actions (schedule follow-up, escalate, flag for review) produced as JSON.

Proposed POC scope (2-week sprint):
1) SDK quickstart repo with Python + TS examples (local run via Docker + env var config).
2) Auth demo: OIDC flow to mint short-lived inference tokens + fallback API-key flow for quick dev.
3) Embeddings baseline: sample pipeline to index 10k anonymized notes, produce embeddings, and run candidate reranking.
4) Structured output example: tool-calling stub that emits a validated JSON schema for triage actions.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart-checklist.pdf (dev steps) and mutual-action-plan.xlsx (roles/timelines).

Immediate asks for your team before we kick off:
- Confirm whether PII/PHI will remain on-prem for the POC or if you can provide a de-identified sample dataset we can use in hosted dev.
- Confirm OIDC provider and whether we can get a dev client for testing (or if you prefer we demo with a short-lived local OIDC shim).
- Preferred dates for a 90-minute technical deep-dive (we suggested a workshop in the call).

If that plan looks good I will loop in Rishi and Marcus to scope the sample apps and provide a repo link + run instructions end of day tomorrow.

Thanks —
Jasmine

Hi all —

Scope and quick plan for the 2-week POC we discussed (technical details below). I created a starter repo and an internal runbook; repo link is in the attachments and Drive.

High-level deliverables (target: 10 business days):
- repo: github.com/redwood-inference/brightpath-poc-samples (Python + TypeScript folders).
- docker-compose dev: local redis (for small vector store), sample web frontend (TS), python worker to call the Redwood SDK.
- Auth: default demo will use a lightweight OIDC shim we host for the POC to emulate Okta SSO. We will also include a documented API-key fallback for quick local dev. For production PHI we recommend Private deployment with Okta OIDC + customer-managed KMS.
- Embeddings + reranker: use mid-sized embedding model (recommended: text-embed-28-small or equivalent) for cost/accuracy tradeoff. Pipeline: embed -> FAISS local index (or Redis Vector) -> candidate rerank using an instruction-tuned model. Estimated peak GPU memory for 5k docs: single inference node (A10G/RTX6000 class) for indexing; low-cost hosted inference for reranking.
- Structured output/tool calling: provide a JSON schema (triage_action) with fields: action_type (schedule/escalate/flag), urgency: {low,medium,high}, patient_id_hash, confidence_score, metadata[]. We'll include a TypeScript validator and a Python pydantic schema in the samples.

Local quickstart (summary):
1) clone repo
2) copy .env.example -> .env and fill: REDWOOD_API_URL, REDWOOD_OIDC_ISSUER (shim), REDWOOD_CLIENT_ID, REDWOOD_API_KEY (fallback), VECTOR_STORE=redis
3) docker-compose up (redis + web + worker)
4) run python scripts/sample_index.py --data=data/deid_notes.json
5) run npm --prefix web start and exercise the sample prompts in web/prompts/clinician.md

Security notes for the POC:
- Do NOT use real PHI in hosted tests. Use de-identified data or run the indexing step locally/on-prem.
- We will include example env configs to switch between hosted and private endpoints.

Attachments we will push by EOD: poc-sampleapps.zip (sample apps + minimalist dataset), runbook.md, and a short prompt set (clinician_prompts.md).

Timeline and owners:
- Day 0–2: repo scaffold + OIDC shim + docker compose (Marcus)
- Day 3–6: embeddings pipeline + sample index scripts (Rishi)
- Day 7–10: web demo + structured output validators + docs (Marissa)

If that looks good I'll push the repo link and drive folder (runbook + attachments) by EOD and book the workshop for one of the slots Emily suggested.

-Rishi
